context: Photoelectric effect: photon completely absorbed by atom; inner-shell electron ejected with kinetic energy E_k = hν - E_binding; cross-section σ_pe ∝ Z^4-5 / E^3.5; rapidly decreasing with energy; increasing with atomic number Z
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: At Chernobyl: Am-241 (59.5 keV gamma) undergoes photoelectric interaction in lead shielding; Ba-137m 662 keV is above photoelectric regime for tissue but Compton-dominant; photoelectric effect explains why lead is excellent gamma shield
source: NIST XCOM database; Attix 1986 Introduction to Radiological Physics; Hubbell 1982

context: Compton scattering: photon scatters off free/loosely-bound electron; photon transfers partial energy to electron; both scatter at angles; cross-section given by Klein-Nishina formula; σ_C decreases with energy at high E; independent of Z (per electron) but depends on electron density
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: Cs-137 662 keV photon: Compton scattering dominant in tissue and air; explains why Cs-137 is detected at long distances; Compton scatter contributes to background at lower energies in gamma spectra; Compton backscatter at 180° gives 184 keV for 662 keV photon
source: Klein O Nishina Y 1929 Z Physik; NIST XCOM; Attix 1986

context: Pair production: photon converts to electron-positron pair in Coulomb field of nucleus; threshold = 2 × m_e × c² = 2 × 0.511 MeV = 1.022 MeV; positron annihilates with electron → two 511 keV annihilation photons
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: Relevant for Co-60 (1.173 + 1.332 MeV): pair production is ~10-20% of total cross-section in tissue at these energies; annihilation peak at 511 keV appears in Co-60 HPGe spectra; not dominant at Cs-137 (662 keV < 1 MeV)

context: Ba-137m (metastable) emits 661.657 keV gamma with 85.1% branching ratio; t1/2(Ba-137m)=2.552 min; in secular equilibrium with Cs-137 in environment; Compton scattering dominant in tissue and common materials at this energy
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: PRIMARY gamma used for Cs-137 detection worldwide; peak at 661.7 keV in NaI or HPGe spectrum IS the Ba-137m gamma; Cs-137 atom itself emits only beta; ALL 662 keV gammas from Chernobyl contamination come from Ba-137m daughter; see radioactive_decay_chains_REAL.csv
source: NNDC NuDat 3; Browne E 1986 Nucl Instrum Methods; radioactive_decay_chains_REAL.csv

context: Cs-134 emits multiple gammas unlike Cs-137 (single dominant peak); t1/2=2.065 yr; fully decayed by ~1992 (10 half-lives after 1986); presence of Cs-134 with Cs-134/Cs-137 ratio ~0.57 was fingerprint of freshly released Chernobyl material
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: Cs-134 presence confirmed Chernobyl origin in April-May 1986 detections globally; ratio 0.57 specific to Unit 4 fuel burnup; gamma spectrometry easily distinguishes Cs-134 from Cs-137 by different peak positions; see atmospheric_transport_plume_REAL.csv

context: I-131 primary gamma 364.5 keV; also 637.0 keV (7.2%), 722.9 keV (1.8%), 284.3 keV (6.1%); photoelectric effect significant at 364.5 keV in dense materials; detected easily by NaI in field measurements
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: I-131 gamma used for field thyroid measurements in 1986 (Soviet DP-100 instruments); however DP-100 was poorly calibrated for neck geometry → factor 3 error in thyroid dose; 364.5 keV also used for thyroid scanning in nuclear medicine (different application)

context: Am-241 emits 59.54 keV gamma (35.9%); low energy = strongly attenuated by soil cover or building materials; photoelectric effect dominant at this energy; detected by low-energy HPGe or NaI but attenuated by >5cm soil; alpha decay predominates (5.486 MeV)
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: Am-241 in CEZ soils NOW (2026): growing from Pu-241 decay; 59.54 keV gamma allows detection of Am-241 in soils with low-energy HPGe; BUT soil depth of >1-2 cm significantly attenuates 59.54 keV; near-surface Am-241 most detectable; see am241_ingrowth_timeseries_REAL.csv

context: Co-60 emits two gammas in cascade (nearly 100% branching); t1/2=5.27 yr; essentially fully decayed by 2026 (99.4%); pair production contributes at these energies; high-energy gammas require thicker shielding than Cs-137
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: Co-60 was major dose contributor 1986-1993; now negligible in CEZ (99.4% decayed); its two-peak signature distinctive in spectrum; used as gamma ray calibration standard in nuclear medicine and radiation protection; reactor_activation_products_REAL.csv has detailed Co-60 data

context: Half-value layer (HVL) in lead at 662 keV: ~6-7 mm; meaning 6-7 mm of Pb reduces Cs-137 gamma intensity by 50%; tenth-value layer (TVL) = 23 mm Pb; shielding calculation: I = I_0 × exp(-µx) where µ = linear attenuation coefficient (cm^-1)
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: For Chernobyl decontamination: 7 mm Pb plate provides 2x reduction in Cs-137 gamma field; 23 mm provides 10x reduction; practical for mobile shielding; heavier shielding needed for high-dose areas near reactor (graphite blocks required meters of concrete/lead)
source: NIST XCOM; Attix 1986; National Council on Radiation Protection; chernobyl_shelter_sarcophagus_REAL.csv

context: HVL in concrete at 662 keV: ~45-60 mm; TVL = ~150-200 mm; concrete density 2.3 g/cm³; standard 20 cm concrete wall provides factor of ~5-10 reduction in Cs-137 gamma
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: Sarcophagus walls: ~50 cm concrete; provides factor 20-100 reduction in Cs-137 gamma from Unit 4; NSC steel provides additional shielding; relevant for dose rates to workers near Shelter; see chernobyl_shelter_sarcophagus_REAL.csv
source: NIST XCOM; Attix 1986; IAEA Safety Reports

context: HVL in tissue/water at 662 keV: ~9 cm; TVL ~30 cm; external Cs-137 gamma: dose mainly deposited in body surface layers; useful for estimating penetrating dose fraction
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: For external contamination dose from skin (from beta vs gamma): Cs-137 beta (max 0.5 MeV) absorbed in ~4mm tissue; 662 keV gamma penetrates deeply and contributes to whole-body dose; explains why external dose model uses ambient H*(10) dosimetric quantity (10 mm depth)

context: NaI(Tl) scintillation detector: thallium-doped sodium iodide crystal; 662 keV photo peak has 7-8% FWHM energy resolution; translates to ~46-53 keV FWHM at 662 keV; adequate for distinguishing Cs-137 (662 keV) from Cs-134 (604 keV) but close call
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: Field gamma spectroscopy at Chernobyl used 3×3 inch NaI probes; can distinguish Cs-137 from I-131 from Co-60 etc.; cannot resolve closely-spaced peaks (e.g., Cs-134 604 keV vs Cs-137 662 keV with NaI); HPGe provides 10-50x better resolution (~0.2% FWHM)
source: Knoll GF Radiation Detection and Measurement 2010; IAEA TECDOC for NaI spectroscopy

context: High-Purity Germanium (HPGe) detector: 0.1-0.3% FWHM at 662 keV = 0.7-2.0 keV FWHM; resolves adjacent peaks easily; requires liquid nitrogen cooling (77K) or mechanical cooling; gold standard for lab gamma spectrometry
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: HPGe used for: laboratory analysis of Chernobyl soil samples; food contamination monitoring; verification of Am-241 in CEZ soils; isotope identification in NRC decommissioning; operational monitoring at CEZ uses portable NaI/CZT with periodic HPGe confirmation
source: Knoll 2010; IAEA Nuclear Analysis Series; retrospective_dosimetry_methods_REAL.csv

context: Compton edge for Cs-137 (662 keV gamma): E_Compton = E_γ × 2α/(1+2α) where α=E_γ/(511 keV)=1.296; E_C = 662 × 2×1.296/(1+2×1.296) = 477.3 keV; in NaI spectrum: continuous Compton continuum 0→477 keV; then gap; then full-energy peak at 662 keV
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: Compton edge and backscatter peak (180° scattered photon at ~184 keV) are characteristic features in every Cs-137 spectrum; understanding spectrum features essential for accurate Cs-137 activity quantification; background subtraction in field measurements

context: Mass attenuation coefficient for 662 keV photon in tissue: µ/ρ = 0.0862 cm²/g; linear attenuation coefficient in tissue (ρ~1 g/cm³): µ = 0.0862 cm^-1; free path length λ=1/µ=11.6 cm; HVL = ln2/µ = 8.0 cm (consistent with 9 cm above)
chernobyl_dosimetry_relevance: For external dose calculation from Cs-137 gamma: I(x) = I_0 × exp(-0.0862x) where x in cm of tissue; dose at depth proportional to energy fluence; builds on dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv 0.0043 µSv/hr per kBq/m² Cs-137 calibration
